reasoning.Student A:
My goal is to maximize my value, given my priority at each school. I have top priority (rank 1) at schools w and y. Since y has a higher value ($72) than w ($58), I prefer y to w. I have priority rank 2 at schools x and z. Since x has a higher value ($52) than z ($53), I prefer x to z.

However, the prompt states that most applicants favor y > x > w > z. This information is irrelevant in the simple view, as I am only concerned with my own values and priorities.

Therefore, my ranking should be based solely on my values and priorities. This means prioritizing schools where I have rank 1, and then ordering within each priority level by value.

Thus, my ranking is y > w > z > x.
